claims.text: The starting materials are crystalline, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles containing five or more metals.
Introducing a small amount of Pt or Pd could enhance the structural stability of these nanoparticles.
Introducing a small amount of Pt or Pd could enhance the chemical stability of these nanoparticles.
The proposed stability enhancement applies during operation at 773–1173 K.
Noble-metal additives can reduce the formation energy of oxygen vacancies.
Noble-metal additives can enhance the mobility of oxygen species.
Reduced oxygen-vacancy formation energy and enhanced oxygen mobility would improve nanoparticle stability.
Noble-metal-modified nanoparticles are predicted to remain more structurally stable than otherwise identical nanoparticles without noble-metal additives.
Noble-metal-modified nanoparticles are predicted to remain more chemically stable than otherwise identical nanoparticles without noble-metal additives.
X-ray diffraction can be used to identify phases during the thermal-exposure experiment.
Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy can be used to assess chemical homogeneity during the thermal-exposure experiment.
Reduced stability or compositional changes in the noble-metal-modified particles during thermal exposure would falsify the hypothesis.
